Hi, thanks for your message, and sorry to hear you're between jobs. I can't go as low as £300, but since you can collect tonight, I could do £350.

So you know what you're getting: it's a 2021 Trek FX 3 Disc, size M. It was serviced in March and had new tyres in June. The gears can be a bit clunky when it's cold, and there's a small tear in the saddle. You're welcome to give it a proper look and a test ride when you come.

That said, £2.55 is well above where we need to be. For an order of 20,000 units, we're looking for a price around £2.20 a unit. At this volume, I'd hope there's room to bring the price down significantly.

Timing matters too: we need the full 20,000 delivered by 1 March. If we can agree on price, I'm keen to get this booked in promptly so you have plenty of lead time.

Could you take another look and let me know what you can do? If it would help, I'm happy to discuss payment terms or scheduling to make the numbers work on your side.

Best regards,
John

Dear Mr Hadley,

Thank you for letting us know, and for being upfront about your costs. We understand things have become more expensive this year, and we're keen to renew for another year.

An increase from £1,250 to £1,450 is a big jump for us, though. It's 16% in one go, and it would stretch our budget considerably.

Over the past three years we've always paid on time, looked after the property, and kept things simple for you. Renewing with us means no empty months, no letting fees, and no uncertainty with new tenants.

With that in mind, could we agree on £1,350 a month for the renewal? We think that's a fair increase that recognises your higher costs, and we'd be happy to sign for another twelve months straight away.

We'd be glad to talk it through if that would help.

Kind regards,
John

Dear Mr Hadley,

An increase from £1,250 to £1,450 is a 16% rise in one go, which is more than we can manage. As you know, we have paid on time every month for the past three years and looked after the property well, so you have had no gaps, arrears or problems with us. We would like to keep that going.

Would you consider £1,325 a month for the renewal? We think that is a fair increase that reflects your higher costs while staying within what we can sustain, and we would be happy to sign promptly so you have certainty for the year ahead.

We are happy to talk it through if that would help.

Best wishes,
John

A few things might help close the gap:

- Delivery is needed by 1 March, but we can be flexible on scheduling before then if that helps you plan production more efficiently.

If you can get closer to that figure, I'm keen to get this booked in quickly.

Best regards,
John

Dear Leo,

Thank you for your message, and for wanting to give "Tidewrack III" a good home. Ines will be glad to hear how much it has stayed with you.

I'm sorry about the tax bill. Unfortunately £2,600 is lower than Ines is able to go for this piece, so I can't say yes at that figure. The listed price is £4,000, but we would be happy to offer it to you for £3,300. If that's still a stretch right now, I'd be glad to ask Ines whether spreading the payment over a few months would help.

There is a faint scuff on the lower left edge of the frame. The canvas itself is unaffected, and I'm happy to send you a close-up photo if you'd like to see it.

Do let me know your thoughts.

Warm regards,
Studio Assistant to Ines

Dear Mrs Okoro,

Thank you for getting back to me, and for being so clear about the board's position. I'd really like to work with you on this project.

My standard day rate is £450, but I'm happy to offer a reduced charity rate of £380 a day. For the full 12 days, that comes to £4,560.

If the board's overall budget is fixed, another option is to keep the total at roughly £3,480 (your 12 days at £290) and adjust the scope instead. At my charity rate, that would cover about 9 days. We could agree together on the most important parts of the work and make sure those are done to a high standard. I work in Figma and Webflow every day, so I can move quickly from design to build and get the most out of the time available.

I'm afraid I can't do the full 12 days at £290, but I hope one of these options works for you and the board. I'm happy to have a quick call to talk through the priorities if that would help.

Best wishes,
John

Dear Mrs Okoro,

Thank you for your message, and for explaining the board's position. I'd very much like to work with you on this project.

My usual day rate is £450. I'm happy to offer a charity rate for your work, but I can't go as low as £290 a day for the full 12 days. I can offer £360 a day, which comes to £4,320 for the project.

If the board can't stretch that far, another option is to adjust the scope so the total fits your budget. We could prioritise the most important parts of the design, and I could set things up in Figma and Webflow so that your team can easily maintain and extend the work later. I'd be glad to go through the brief with you to see what's essential.

Please let me know which option works best for you, and I'll be happy to talk it through.

Best wishes,
John

Please let me know which approach suits you best, and I'll be glad to get started.

Best wishes,
John

Hi,

Thank you for your offer, and we're so pleased you love the house. Being first-time buyers with no chain is a real advantage, and we'd very much like to make this work with you.

Unfortunately we can't accept £378,000. The house is priced at £415,000, and that reflects the new kitchen fitted in 2023 and the south-facing garden. However, we're keen to find a figure that works for both of us, so we'd be willing to come down to £395,000.

We understand your mortgage offer is your limit. Would it be possible to check whether there's any flexibility on your deposit, or whether your lender could look again at the amount? If you can get closer to our figure, we'd be happy to move forward quickly.

Let us know what you think.

Best wishes

Hi,

Thank you for your offer, and we're so pleased you love the house.

We've thought carefully about £378,000, but unfortunately it's further below the asking price than we're able to go. The kitchen was fitted new in 2023, and the south-facing garden is one of the things we'll miss most.

We'd like to make this work for you, so we'd be willing to accept £398,000. It may also help to know that we've already secured our next home, so there's no onward chain on our side and we can move at a pace that suits you.

We understand your mortgage offer sets a limit. It might be worth checking with your broker or lender whether there's any flexibility, or whether a slightly larger deposit could close the gap. We're happy to talk it through if that would help.

We look forward to hearing from you.

Best wishes

Hi,

Thank you for your offer, and we're really glad you love the house. It's lovely to hear that from first-time buyers.

We've thought about it carefully, but we're not able to accept £378,000. The house is on at £415,000, and we feel that reflects the new kitchen fitted in 2023 and the south-facing garden. We do want to find a way to make this work with you, though, so we'd be happy to come down to £390,000.

We've already bought our next home, so there's no onward chain on our side. That means we can move at whatever pace suits you and your lender.

If £378,000 is the limit of your mortgage, it may be worth checking with your broker whether there's any flexibility, or whether you could cover the difference from savings. If you'd like to come back for a second viewing before deciding, you'd be very welcome.

Kind regards
